Getting started with the Widget API

The Widget API is a small HTTP service for creating and listing widgets. Every request needs an API key, passed in the X-Api-Key header. Keys are issued per project and can be rotated at any time without downtime.

Creating a widget

Send a POST request to /v1/widgets with a JSON body containing a name and an optional colour. The response carries the new widget id, which you will need for every later call about that widget.

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/widgets \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -d '{"name": "left-handed sprocket"}'

Listing widgets

A GET request to /v1/widgets returns your widgets, newest first, twenty per page. Pass ?cursor= with the cursor from the previous response to walk the rest of the list. An empty list means you have reached the end.

Errors

Errors use standard status codes. A 401 means the key is missing or wrong, a 404 means the widget id does not exist, and a 429 means you are sending requests faster than the plan allows. The body always contains a machine-readable code.
